correctness.rationale: For \(m=5\), every signed residual has denominator dividing 60 and numerator \(A=12-60w_1-30w_2-20w_3-15w_4\). Independent exact enumeration of all 81 coefficient choices reproduced the repository's 32 absolute reduced numerators and their complete prime-divisor union, with maximum numerator 137. Thus every prime above 137 is automatically compatible and the ten compatible primes through 137 are exactly the displayed list. The propagation proof is a correct p-adic localization argument: after isolating indices divisible by \(p^k\), every remaining term has positive p-adic valuation after multiplication, forcing p to divide the reduced residual numerator, contradicting compatibility. The final doubling equivalence follows directly from the two translates defining \(E_N\).

Its text explicitly exhibits one exceptional low prime for seed 4, not the complete low-prime spectrum for seed 5. The audited 81-case exact census therefore refines, rather than restates, the published mechanism. Resultary returned the assigned finding as the only direct exact hit.

value.rationale: The seed \(m=5\) is not arbitrary: it is explicitly used in the current recursive lower-bound construction with the coarse threshold 137. Computing its exact compatibility spectrum identifies every low-prime exception and converts nine of them into infinite doubling rays. Even without changing the leading asymptotic constant, this is a natural exact local invariant of the published mechanism and can support sharper finite or hybrid constructions.
residual_risks: The finite refinement has limited asymptotic impact by itself.

final_claim: For the Bettin--Grenié--Molteni--Sanna compatibility notion at the seed \(m=5\), the compatible primes are exactly \(\{5,59,71,79,89,101,103,109,127,131\}\cup\{p\text{ prime}:p>137\}\); each of the nine mixed primes below 137 therefore gives \(5p^k\in\mathcal U\) and \(|E_{5p^k}|=2|E_{5p^k-1}|\) for every \(k\ge1\).
limitations: Exact classification for the single seed m=5 only.
The nine additional prime rays do not by themselves improve the leading asymptotic constant in the cited lower bound.
